13386.html:
13386 síkatā f. 'grain of sand', (usu. pl.) 'sand, gravel' VS., sigatā- f. Kap. [Collective formation from sika- in śvēta-sika-druka- 'scattering white sand' TĀr. 1. 12. 3 A. Sharma in Bhārata-kaumudī 873. Kaf. and some Dard. forms attest IA. ś- corresponding to Ir. θ- and s- (OPers. θikā-, Bal. six, Psht. šəga, &c. EVP 73) and support E. Benveniste BSL xxx 60 in assumption that s- forms of Sk. and other Dard. languages and WPah. (which distinguish ś and s) are loans from or influenced by Iranian. Variations in Kaf. and Dard. of -g- ~ -k- and -l- ~ -t- may be due to borrowings within that group or to later Ir. influences or they may, in part at least, be due to suffix. variation like that of síkatā- ~ *sikatī- (in sikatyà- VS.) ~ siktā- lex. ~ *sikyā-]
    *śikatā-: Kt. ċü, ċüyü 'sand', Wg. šō, Ash. šō̃ṛə, Dm. ċī˜a, Kho. šuγúr (< earlier *šiguδ → Kal.rumb. šīgou, st. šīgol-, urt. šigər).
    síkatā: Pa. sikatā- f. 'sand, gravel', NiDoc. siǵataṁmi loc. sg.; Pk. sikayā-, sigayā- f. 'sand', Paš.dar. sē̆o, chil. sīóu, kuṛ. sīu, ar. siō, Shum. sī́u, Gaw. sī́ũ; — ← Ir. dialect preserving -t- (?): Woṭ. sigit f. (šigit infl. by Psht. šəga Buddruss Woṭ 126), Bshk. sigit f.
    *sikyā-, *sikyatā- (cf. Ir. *sikya- E. Benveniste loc. cit.): K. sĕkh, dat. sĕki f. 'sand, file' (semant. cf. rētra-); WPah.khaś. sikk 'gravel', bhal. sikkā f.
    Ext. -l- (cf. sikatilá- 'sandy' Bhartr̥.) perh. in Kt. ċele 'sand', Paš.lauṛ. siyēl m., gul. sēl m. IIFL iii 3, 161, Tor. sigλ'l m., Chil. Gau. sigil, Sv. šigala (š- from Psht. šəga → Phal. šíga f. NOPhal 48); Phal. sígλl m. 'fine sand'; Sh.gil. sĭgăl m. 'sand', pales. sλgλl.
    sikatilá- see síkatā-.
    Addenda: síkatā-: x śarkarā-¹ (Pk. sikkarā-) Add²; poss. also in Pk. sikayā-, K. sēk-, WPah. sikk, sikkā.
